summary: Round 2 re-review after the mini repair. The round-1 major (abdominal auscultation rationale) is fixed: the lesson, summary, q001 and its explanation now correctly say some schools auscultate before palpation because touch may alter bowel sounds, while many UK OSCE schemes auscultate after, and to follow the local scheme. The other five repaired units (guarding definition, pulse-count consistency, pulse threshold in q006, tourniquet escalation in first aid, documentation q001) are fixed and introduced no new errors; BLS, AED, choking, bleeding and recovery-position content is consistent with UK Resuscitation Council guidance. All numeric keys (pack-years, units, deoxy-Hb, blood volume/loss, compression time/fraction, liver span, compliance, time differences, pulse and respiratory rates) were recomputed and are correct, and every MCQ has exactly one correct option matching the key. Remaining findings are five minor items: a clinically unrealistic liver-span stem, escaped unicode literals in the vital-signs unit, and small scope/consistency gaps. This is an AI review only; the course still needs a subject-matter expert before clinical reliance.

issues.problem: Unicode escapes are stored as literal text and will display raw, for example "60\u2013100 beats/min", "12\u201320 breaths/min", "36.0\u201337.5\u00b0C" in the lesson table and body text, "12 cm \u00d7 23 cm" in the cuff worked example, "9 cm \u00d7 18 cm" in q004 options, "36.9\u00b0C" in q007 options, and "38.2\u00b0C" in q010 and its marking guide.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the literal \uXXXX sequences with the actual characters (en dash, multiplication sign, degree sign) throughout the lesson blocks, options and marking guides of this unit, then check that the page renders correctly.

issues.problem: Stem says "the upper limit of dullness is 5.2 cm and the lower limit is 12.2 cm below the costal margin". The upper limit of liver dullness lies in the 5th-6th intercostal space, above the costal margin, and a lower border 12.2 cm below the margin would be massive hepatomegaly. The arithmetic key of 7 cm is right, but the stem describes an anatomically unrealistic measurement.
issues.suggestedFix: Reword so both limits are measured along the right midclavicular line (for example upper dullness at the 5th intercostal space, lower dullness at the costal margin, with the distances given in cm from a stated reference), or simply state upper and lower limits of 5.2 and 12.2 cm measured along the midclavicular line, without referring to the costal margin.

issues.problem: The marking guide expects structures not given in the lesson and assigns some differently: hepatic flexure, tail of pancreas, aorta in the umbilical region, and sigmoid colon in the hypogastrium, whereas the lesson places sigmoid colon in the left iliac fossa and lists bladder and uterus only for the hypogastrium.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the marking guide with the lesson, or add the extra structures to the lesson, and accept either region for overlapping organs such as the sigmoid colon.

issues.problem: Marking guide includes "Pelvic examination may be required in selected patients with appropriate consent and training", which is not in the lesson and is beyond Year 1 clinical skills scope for an unobserved intimate examination.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the pelvic examination item, or present it only as something done by trained clinicians; keep the expected answer to external genital and digital rectal examination as taught in the lesson.

issues.problem: The question identifies S1 using timing with the carotid pulse upstroke, but the lesson never teaches timing of heart sounds against the carotid pulse. The objective to identify S1 and S2 is covered in the lesson only by mechanism and location.
issues.suggestedFix: Add one or two lines to the lesson explaining that S1 coincides with the carotid upstroke and is followed by systole, with S2 following, or reword the stem to rely on location and mechanism only.

issues.problem: The first worked example's model note adds "No dyspnoea or difficulty swallowing" to the history, which is not in the stem; the unit teaches that notes should record only what was actually elicited or observed.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the invented negatives from the model answer (and the matching table example), or add them to the prompt as findings the student elicited.
